sentences.text: The Qian family's courtyard was very old, a traditional quadrangle courtyard.
Despite its age, it was spacious.
Walking from the front door to the backyard took at least fifteen minutes, and that was just walking.
The receptionist was a well-dressed middle-aged woman.
She wasn't particularly beautiful, but she had a gentle demeanor and the aura of a wealthy noblewoman.
"Sister-in-law, this is Zhao An.
Zhao An, this is my sister-in-law, Xu Yan." Qian Yuling introduced them.
"Well, Zhao An, I've heard of you for a long time, and seeing you today is indeed quite impressive.
Come, I've prepared a room for you.
Rest up first; dinner will be starting soon." Xu Yan smiled gently.
As the wife of the head of the family, her personal greeting conveyed her respect.
"Very good, Auntie is very beautiful." Zhao An extended his hand and shook it, nodding slightly.
His smile was gentle, another classic con man.
As the group moved forward, Xu Yan noticed that several people's suitcases were high-tech.
As the person walked in front, the suitcase followed behind, seemingly controlled by a remote control.
"Your suitcases are very unique," Xu Yan exclaimed, a hint of curiosity in her.
"It's just a small invention, nothing to mention." Zhao An smiled, but didn't continue to introduce it.
He was showing off without telling the other party, acting mysterious.
Xu Yan had arranged three rooms, but Qian Yuling placed the suitcase in Zhao An's room.
"Just give us one room.
I'll go see Mom."
"Okay, I'll take you there." Xu Yan was only slightly stunned, stunned by the fact that her sister-in-law Qian Yuling would so willingly sleep in the same room with a man.
Remember, before the Tang family collapsed, Qian Yuling and her husband also slept in separate rooms when they returned.
This was quite interesting.
Zhao An had wanted to finalize the business deal first, but then he glanced at Qian Yuling's expression and said nothing.
Instead, he followed her on.
The left side of the courtyard was deserted, with only a few elderly people occasionally strolling around.
The interior was neatly decorated, with no unnecessary ornamentation.
The pale white walls, accented by a few windows from the last century, gave it a retro feel.
It was retro yet stylish, creating a tranquil atmosphere.
"This is a very nice place to rest and recuperate," Zhao An suddenly exclaimed, commenting.
"This place was originally built for the elderly.
The older generation of the Qian family lived here.
There aren't many people here, but each one was a prominent figure in the last century," Qian Yuling explained, occasionally greeting passersby.
"They've retired, but their connections remain.
Even in their old age, their dedication is still very useful," Qian Yuling continued, explaining to her young husband.
She had just been fucked for two hours on the plane, and now, aside from her rosy complexion, she walked without a tremor, giving no sign that her womb was still filled with Zhao An's semen.
"That's what they say: 'An old man in the family is like a treasure,'" Zhao An nodded.
The old man's connections, or rather, those of the older generation, still proved useful.
Sometimes, the favor of helping someone lasted as long as the old man lived.
It was a form of awe, a kind of honor, and a form of intimidation.
We passed through a bamboo garden, planted with evergreen bamboo.
Circles of stone slabs lay beneath, with raised pebbles on the sides, used for foot massage.
It was clear from the ground that this was indeed a retirement home, a place for the elderly to keep fit.
We arrived at a rather modern two-story building, where servants were cleaning.
Zhao An looked around, and after seeing no signs of an ambush or any other such spectacle, he followed Qian Yuling forward.
The room contained a large pit, with a modern stove underneath.
A little coal added to the stove provided warmth at night.
The unique design also avoids the risk of excessive carbon dioxide poisoning.
This old-fashioned, retro item doesn't feel outdated.
A woman with silver hair sat in a chair, reading a newspaper, wearing a pair of gold-rimmed glasses.
At first glance, she looked a bit like a different kind of young person, her skin well-maintained, though a few crow's feet at the corners of her eyes hinted at her age.
She didn't look old, though, more like a stylish middle-aged woman.
Qian Yuling looked at the woman before her, her lips moving.
"Mom, this is Zhao An.
Zhao An, this is my mother, Zheng Peiyi."
"Hello, Madam Qian." Zhao An nodded and glanced at Qian Yuling.
His usual dominance seemed lost, a hint of aggrievedness and a touch of fear.
Zheng Peiyi put down the newspaper, a touch of light lipstick on her lips, looking refreshed.
"Glad to be back," she turned to Zhao An.
"You're quite good, young man."
"You're sick!" Zhao An suddenly exclaimed.
Qian Yuling and Xu Yan both looked at Zhao An in surprise.
Qian Yuling tugged at her husband, "What are you talking about?"
"I said your mother is ill, and seriously ill," Zhao An said, looking into Qian Yuling's eyes.
Then he looked at the beautiful, silver-haired woman before him.
Despite her excellent care, time had spared no one.
Even if she looked ageless, she had already reached the level of a middle-aged woman, which was quite extraordinary.
"Zhao An, don't talk nonsense.
My mother-in-law isn't ill.
You're being rude," Xu Yan snapped.
This sudden incident was a slap in the face.
Only Zheng Peiyi maintained a smile, unperturbed by the words.
"You're right, I'm ill.
Do you know what it is?"
"The whites of your eyes are dim, your lips are slightly cracked, and your right index and middle fingers are slightly yellowed.
Your steps are slightly shaky, and your eyesight is unfocused.
You have a lot of problems.
Have you been feeling dizzy lately?

You sweat profusely at night, and your sleep quality isn't good." Zhao An spoke eloquently, having instantly identified something wrong.

chapters.title: Chapter 684 Acupuncture treatment!
paragraphs: Zheng Peiyi put down the newspaper and clapped her hands. "Not bad, very impressive. You're quite knowledgeable about medicine, worthy of being a descendant of the Bai family."

"This has nothing to do with whether or not I'm from the Bai family. I have no connection to the Bai family either," Zhao An snorted. Everything he did was given by the system and earned through his own hard work. It had nothing to do with anyone else. He hated this kind of forced fraud.
"Okay, young man, you're very energetic. Do you know how to treat it?" Zheng Peiyi continued, her smile still gentle.
"I never do business at a loss," Zhao An waved his hand, treating everyone the same.

Qian Yuling fell silent. It turned out her young husband truly understood medical principles. She had seemed a little irrational just now, and she might be in trouble again tonight. A beautiful woman suffers, a handsome man suffers.
"What do you want?" Zheng Peiyi said with a smile that looked kind, yet also tinged with a hint of arrogance.
"It's not about what I want, but what you can give." Zhao An sat nonchalantly aside, lighting a cigarette and taking a drag.

"I feel very confident that Yuling is with you. Can't you help an old woman like me?" Zheng Peiyi's face was still full of smiles, her words flawless. She pointed out the relationship between the two and then placed herself in a position of superiority, acting a bit like a senior.

"Yuling is my wife, what does it have to do with you? You make it sound like you've done a lot." Zhao An was not polite. Want to take advantage? Look who he is! Want to morally blackmail him? I'll break his legs in a second!

This statement surprised Xu Yan, who was standing beside her. She didn't show any displeasure at all. She was just watching the show, as if she wanted to see what tricks the old lady, who was strategizing, could come up with.

"Yuling is my daughter. What does that have to do with me? I raised her. You just picked her up ready-made. Isn't that good enough?" Zheng Peiyi countered, still smiling. Even her arguments were gentle and gentle, like a spring breeze, making it impossible to get angry. This was her brilliance: she suppressed the negotiating partner's aura.
"You really like getting something for nothing. Amazing! You're worthy of being called the Iron Lady." Zhao An clapped his hands, then said, "Hold out your hand. I'll take your pulse."
There was no politeness in his tone, and a hint of impatience.

Zheng Peiyi knew that she could only suppress the other party because he didn't want to argue with her. What right did a patient have to negotiate with a doctor? "Okay, thank you. Yan, go get Xiao An a cup of tea."
The tone of the words suddenly changed to a friendly one. This is how big families are: one moment it's Zhao An, the next it's Xiao An, and they change their minds faster than the pages of a book.
Qian Yuling didn't say anything, but stood behind Zhao An, taking a deep drag on her cigarette, looking both annoyed and depressed.
His fingers rested on his veins, Zhao An narrowed his eyes, tapping one hand on the table, as if calculating something.
After a minute, Zhao An released his hand. "Want faster or slower?"
"A treatment method?" Zheng Peiyi replied softly, barely keeping up with Zhao An's pace.
"What else do you think?" Zhao An took another drag on his cigarette, his eyes fixed on the table, seemingly lost in thought.
"You're going back tomorrow, right?" Zheng Peiyi's expression darkened.

"Yes, tomorrow," Qian Yuling answered for her young husband. She had mixed feelings about her mother. Zheng Peiyi had taught her how to be a strong woman, how not to be treated as a plaything by men, that was certain. It was just that she lacked the motherly affection, which was why her expression was a little complicated.
"Then let's use a faster method." Zheng Peiyi quickly made up her mind.

"This requires a combination of medicine and acupuncture, which is very expensive. But since you're my cheap mother-in-law, I'll make an exception and give you this once." Zhao An then pulled out a bag of silver needles from behind his back, no one knew where they came from.
"Are you good at acupuncture? I've never seen you do it before," Qian Yuling asked suspiciously, her question addressed to her mother.
Pa! Zhao An slapped Qian Yuling's hip in front of the two of them. "Don't you know how capable your husband is?"
Qian Yuling covered her hip, her pretty face flushed. This scene rarely made her feel shy. "You have to cure my mom. She's had asthma for years."

Zheng Peiyi smiled as she watched her daughter flirting with Zhao An. Despite the age difference between them, her daughter was the one getting the upper hand. An older man taking advantage of a younger woman was definitely a thrilling and pleasurable experience.
Xu Yan remained silent, pretending to be oblivious to what was happening outside. There was no need for her to get involved; she could simply remain invisible.

Zhao An quickly texted the prescription to Xu Yan's phone. "Sister-in-law, go get the medicine. The acupuncture treatment takes two hours, so it's best to start now. Afterward, eat to replenish your nutrients and rest for a night. You'll be free of illness the next day."
Xu Yan glanced at Zheng Peiyi, who nodded. "Do as he say."
Qian Yuling felt the atmosphere was a bit strange, so she picked up her handbag and followed Xu Yan out. "Honey, you give my mom acupuncture. I'll go talk to my brother about the partnership."

Qian Yuling breathed a sigh of relief after leaving the house. Without seeing her mother, her aura suddenly changed. Her eyes gleamed with pride and determination, transforming her into the alluring, sexy, powerful woman who made people drool.
Xu Yan asked curiously, "Yuling, are you really with Zhao An?"

"Is there anything wrong with that?" Qian Yuling asked back. She didn't think it was wrong at all; it was actually quite good. The surging passion of a young man, coupled with the long-suffering lust of a mature woman, a raging fire, a collision of dry wood and fervent passion, how could it not explode?
Xu Yan shook her head. "It's nothing. I wish you happiness. You're so lucky to finally be living a normal life. I'm so happy for you."

"Thank you. Of all the family members, you're the most articulate. Thank you, sister-in-law." Qian Yuling looked down upon the Qian family's children. Only a few knew how to behave, and sister-in-law Xu Yan was one of them.

chapters.title: Chapter 685 The rules of the Qian family?
paragraphs: Zhao An picked up a silver needle and placed it over an alcohol lamp to sterilize it. The slender needle gleamed with a hint of coldness. "Aren't you afraid I might harm you?"

Zheng Peiling smiled kindly. "I'm an old man, what is there to fear? I've lived enough." There was a lightness and indifference in her words, as if she had seen through the mundane world and was free from all worries.
"Really? Then why do you want treatment? Do you want to live longer, or perhaps maintain your youthful beauty?" Zhao An said expressionlessly, his eyes fixed on the needle.

This was the first time he had used his medical skills, which he had learned long ago. When he first got the system, Zhao An spent almost all his time in the city library, where a vast amount of knowledge was stored.
He studied so hard, not for grades, but to unlock the knowledge within. It's no exaggeration to call Zhao An a master of all trades now. He knows everything, masters everything.
Was all that hard work done in the early days just to show off? No, it was to enjoy life in this moment.

The decision to save Zheng Peiyi wasn't a sudden decision; it was planned long ago. It just so happened that this time, they encountered Qian Yuling's mother. The target wasn't important; what mattered was that this person had to hold a certain level of influence within their family.

Old people are afraid of death, so making some concessions to prolong their lives is perfectly normal. And the family wouldn't let them die so quickly. The elders are spiritual symbols. Often, not taking action means the elders' affections are still there; if they did, it would be chaos.
This time, it was just to establish his reputation. Want him to save her in the future? Sure, pay me, I'll save her. No? Then die.
Taking a deep puff of his cigarette, Zhao An looked at Zheng Peiyi, who was smiling at him. He remained silent, using silence to mask his guilt. "Take off your clothes."
"Okay." Zheng Peiyi wasn't shy. She took off her clothes openly, leaving only her underwear, revealing her fair skin. It was quite good, well-maintained for her age.

Zhao An focused on acupuncture and massage for Zheng Peiyi, simultaneously dispersing qi. He expelled accumulated toxins from the body while stimulating the organs through acupuncture points, revitalizing them.
Only when the internal organs are healthy can the body be healthy. This was medical treatment, not pornography.

"Xiao An, please promise me one thing. Treat Yuling well. I will personally train her to be a useful person. She wasn't happy before, and had to marry into the Tang family to keep the family line going. Now, I see she's happy with you. Treat her well, and she'll be a good wife, a good mother, and a good helper!" Zheng Peiyi squinted her eyes. The massage was truly pleasurable.

"I would do it even if you didn't tell me. She's my woman, my wife. Aside from the lack of a marriage certificate, she's no different from my wife. I'll let her bear me children. Don't worry." Zhao An performed the massage with a focused gaze.
It's not impossible to use medical skills to save lives, but it requires extreme concentration. Surgery is no joke. Pressing the wrong acupoint can cause serious trouble.
Two hours later, Zhao An washed his hands, still stained with a little blood.
"Alright, let's eat now, then get some sleep. Tomorrow you'll notice something different." Zhao An wiped his hands clean, his expression remaining calm.
Xu Yan, who was waiting, helped her mother-in-law to her feet. Zheng Peiyi's face flushed red, her energy returning. However, there was a pungent odor, coated in a kind of excrement.
These were accumulated toxins. As cells age, their function declines. Ultimately, the toxins accumulate, forming age spots, depleting nutrients, and ultimately accelerating death.
"Thank you." Zheng Peiling's gratitude was sincere this time, without a trace of falsehood. She truly felt well and comfortable.
"Go take a shower! I'm starving. Let's have dinner soon," Zhao An said, hugging Qian Yuling, who had hurried over. He was indeed hungry.
"Thank you, husband," Qian Yuling whispered.
"Words like that are useless. Let's show some real action. Just thank me properly tonight!" Zhao An smirked. Actual benefits moved people more than empty promises.
"Okay, whatever you want tonight," Qian Yuling replied quietly, her heart overflowing with love for Zhao An.
What surprised Zhao An was that even though it was already eight o'clock, everyone in the living room was waiting for him to eat.
A middle-aged man, slightly balding, with a calm demeanor, sat at the main table. "Zhao An, take this way," he said, invitingly gesturing from the seat next to him.
The young people present were a little surprised, wondering how someone so much younger than them could hold such a position of power.
Many of the men's eyes lit up when they saw Qian Yuling. This woman was a legend, a beautiful legend.
Zhao An didn't refuse, pulling Qian Yuling to their seat. "You weren't waiting for me, were you? I think you were waiting for Madam Zheng."
"Haha, I was waiting for you. Thank you for treating my mother. She's the pillar of our family. Let me toast you!" Qian Ben took his glass and emptied it.

Zhao An also took his glass and emptied it. "You're welcome. This time it's free, but next time I'll have to charge. Besides, I don't usually treat people. Their lives are of no concern to me. I have no interest in saving lives."
"Haha, you're such a true man. Come on, please!" Qian Ben gestured as if to invite them to eat, then shouted to the other tables, "Eat!"
Only after Qian Ben spoke did anyone else dare to pick up their chopsticks. That was the rule. Without rules, there's no order.
Zhao An smiled, not being polite, but quickly picking up his food. The meal was plentiful—not quite a full banquet, but at least a third of it. It was already quite a feast.
Lotus seed soup, rich fish, golden steamed buns, and so on—all delicacies embodying regional characteristics.
Zhao An accepted everything, unpicky about the food and seemingly unfamiliar with it, and simply began to eat.
Embarrassed? That's a childish emotion. Being shy means you can't eat enough. Why would you go against your own appetite just to save face?

Embarrassed?

Being shy means you can't eat enough.

paragraphs: Large families do have a lot of rules, especially when it comes to dining. The saying "no rules, no order" seems a bit of a stretch.

Zhao An noticed something interesting about the seating arrangements. Women sat with women, men with men. Young people sat at one table, while the older generation sat at another, practically dividing the dining area by age.
The unique seating arrangement only made Zhao An realize how many ridiculously large family rules there were, but it didn't affect his eating speed.
Watching Zhao An devour his meal, the Qian family's core management staff were all puzzled and astonished. Had this guy been hungry for three days?

"Good appetite! I envy you young people." Qian Ben took a sip of his red wine. He was used to this kind of thing. As the head of a family, he should remain calm even in the face of adversity, remaining unperturbed by praise or criticism. Only then could he project a calm demeanor to those below him.

"Being able to eat proves good health. Without a healthy body, making a lot of money is meaningless." Zhao An was already full. He had practically devoured the entire meal, leaving others to eat only his leftovers.

"Indeed, I wonder what your thoughts are on future developments?" Qian Ben suddenly asked a slightly crucial question, one that made most people pause and listen intently. This was about making money, and this kind of information was worth a fortune!

Zhao An took out a cigarette and lit it, unfazed. "The future is the internet age. Whether it's mobile or fixed internet, it's the unstoppable trend. I prefer mobile internet. With the development and upgrading of mobile phones, the internet's methods can disrupt traditional industries. It's just that most people only see the surface, not the underlying essence."
"What is the underlying essence?" asked a bespectacled family member, dressed in a suit, leather shoes, and shorts, looking truly respectable.
Zhao An glanced at him. "Inner nature is the key to making money. I won't elaborate on that. Just explore it on your own."

"This!" Everyone was stunned. Was he kidding? It had come to this point. It was like soliciting prostitution. The prostitute was already at the hotel entrance, and you said you didn't want to play anymore? Isn't this a complete joke?
Qian Yuling couldn't help but laugh. She knew this was just male nature. He'd saved her mother out of respect, but he wouldn't necessarily treat the other members of the Qian family the same way.

"A few words won't hurt. Just think of it as a little inspiration for the younger generation of the Qian family. They all think of you as a star, a true genius." Qian Ben offered kind words. This was a rare opportunity, and if Zhao An could say a few more words, it would be a great inspiration to the Qian family members.

Feeling the gazes of the Qian family members present, Zhao An remained unmoved. He blew out a smoke ring, and the hall was filled with the aroma of medicinal herbs. Everyone, who had initially thought it was the stink of cigarettes, was also surprised. This cigarette seemed to have something special.
Zhao An took out a cigarette and handed it to Qian Ben. "I won't give it away. This one costs two hundred thousand."
This made everyone's eyelids raise. Two hundred thousand for a cigarette?

It wasn't that they couldn't afford it, but that it wasn't necessary. They were all coal bosses, so how could they be short of money? Even coal bosses wouldn't be fooled. If they spent two hundred thousand on a minor celebrity, it would be considered great value. But two hundred thousand for a cigarette, for a matter of just one minute—that was a bit unreasonable.

"I recommend not smoking this kind of cigarette. It helps quit smoking. After you smoke this kind of cigarette, other cigarettes will become boring. So if you want to quit, give it a try. If you don't, don't try it." Zhao An puffed on his cigarette, one hand resting on the table, giving off a somewhat frivolous air.

"So, what are your thoughts on the development of the internet?" Qian Ben brought the conversation back to making money. If Zhao An weren't such a genius, he certainly wouldn't have continued to dwell on the issue.

Zhao An's eyes hinted at a hint of amusement. "Old Qian, I'll show you a clear path. Don't worry about internet trends. Focus on the logistics industry. I guarantee you'll still be profitable in the next 30 years. Not fabulously wealthy, but certainly enough to keep your Qian family on par with the rest of the pack."

"Don't say I'm not looking out for you. I wouldn't say that about ordinary people. Of course, a corresponding upgrade is necessary. Keep up with mobile internet trends and develop appropriate software to ensure you don't get left behind," Zhao An added, his smile enigmatic.
This statement made everyone present's eyes light up. It was obvious: just focus on the logistics industry.
If Zhao An hadn't created the mythical legend of earning tens of billions a month, no one would have paid any attention to what he said.

Qian Yuling sat nearby, calmly drinking her red wine, her expression unwavering. In reality, she was already feeling a little soft inside. She could feel the heat welling up inside her, eager to make love with Zhao An, the now talkative and powerful man, to mate with him, to let her young husband fuck her hard.
The reason was simple: Zhao An was just too handsome. A serious man at this moment was the most attractive.

As Zhao An and Qian Ben disappeared from view, the living room returned to its lively atmosphere.

Some of the women in the Qian family began to pull Qian Yuling over to get close to them. They had mocked her when she was in debt. It was simply because Qian Yuling was so beautiful that they were jealous.
Now that Qian Yuling had become Zhao An's trusted partner, these female relatives changed their expressions again, one after another, wearing fawning smiles.

They weren't fools; they knew Qian Yuling was definitely making a lot of money, especially now that her new smartphone had already started shipping. Everyone who had used it praised it, and the price was very affordable, just 1,999 yuan, less than 2,000 yuan. Its performance far surpassed those phones costing 3,000 or 4,000 yuan, and its quality and affordability made it highly competitive.

paragraphs: No one knew what Zhao An and Qian Ben were conspiring to do. All they knew was that their conversation lasted only half an hour, and when they emerged, they were arm in arm, practically sworn brothers.
"Then it's settled," Qian Ben said, shaking hands.

"Print out the contract and begin the logistics process. I'll send someone to sign the contract. Okay, now that we've finished the real business, let's leave it at that." Zhao An appeared nonchalant, leaving the difficult task to the Qian family.

In the transportation industry, it would be no easy task for the Fang family to take on these coal bosses. The Qian family was a local tyrant, and their long-established network of influence was formidable. Any attempt by the Fang family to take on the Qian family would mean making more enemies.
As for finding faults with the product, they were welcome to do so.
"Understood. I'll arrange it now." Qian Ben nodded eagerly, knowing that according to Zhao An, he could remain head of the family for at least ten years!
"Go ahead, I'll go take a walk around on my own," Zhao An waved his hand. As a man of high rank, he was no longer the poor wretch who couldn't even afford prostitutes.
The Qian family's courtyard was large. Zhao An had only taken a few steps when he saw a man in his thirties walking straight towards him. He greeted him from a distance, "Mr. Zhao!"
The man wore glasses and looked somewhat refined. "Hello, Mr. Zhao. I'm Qian Haoming. Qian Ben is my father. Let me show you around our night market tonight."
"Well, just call me by my first name, or you can call me Young Master An," Zhao An said with a gentle smile.

Given Zhao An's current status and age, there was nothing wrong with calling him Zhao An. But Qian Haoming was a shrewd man, and calling him that would irritate him. There was no need to offend him just to save face. "Young Master An, please come this way."
In addition to Qian Haoming, there were two other men following him: one burly and strong, the other a bit thin, looking a bit like a military advisor.
"Not bad, two henchmen, one civil and one military. They have some connections, not bad," Zhao An commented briefly.

"You're too polite, Mr. An. These are my two cousins. Thanks to their help, I can handle company affairs with peace of mind." Qian Haoming was clearly very good at dealing with people, and he'd enlisted his cousins' help, which was quite impressive.

"Just telling the truth." Zhao An turned to look out the window. After leaving the residence, the road was quiet for a while, yet not deserted. There were also houses outside, all two- or three-story suites, perfect for families.
As the car gradually moved, they arrived in the city. Here, one could see supermarkets, bustling shopping districts, and a pedestrian street.

"Mr. An, are you interested in having a drink at the bar?" Qian Haoming asked, his airs low. As a host, his duty was to ensure his guests had a good time. As for women, there was no need to deliberately offer them. His aunt was very beautiful and sexy, so there was no need to bother with her.
But as the saying goes, wild flowers are always more fragrant than domesticated ones. Some people do enjoy playing with women outside, like both of them, father and son.
"No, I rarely go to bars. They're boring after a while. I just want to hang out." Zhao An had no such interest or hobby.

You say you're going to bars to pick up girls? Do you really think there are so many innocent women out there? They're all those who enjoy being promiscuous. Who would go to a bar with a decent person? At most, they'd just go for a drink in a bar. Bars filled with heavy metal music are never that fun.

"What are Young An's hobbies? Can I arrange that? Or do you want to see the museums here?" Qian Haoming was a little unsure. This lecherous guy wouldn't even go to bars to play with women? What the hell? A pervert with no interest in women?

"Not really. My hobby is spending money on women. What's the point of making money? To support a family? That's half right. It's more about enjoying life. Stop ahead. I want to see what's in the museum." A playful smile curled Zhao An's lips.
Rather than playing with those sluts, whores who'd been fucked by countless men, he'd rather find other entertainment.
The museum was closed at night, but that wasn't a problem for Qian Haoming. As a local tycoon, he could easily get someone to open the door with just a phone call.
This was an ancient museum, displaying Bronze Age artifacts and ancient documents.
As soon as Zhao An entered, he noticed something amiss. The ancient artifacts seemed to shimmer slightly. Some didn't, while most did, with a few not. This was odd.
And without the lights on, there was no way any of the artifacts would shimmer.
"Young Master An, this is an ancient museum, renovated in modern times. It houses many artifacts, all protected," Qian Haoming explained, cautioning Zhao An against any further attempts.
"Are these genuine antiques?" Zhao An didn't approach, but watched from a distance, a thoughtful look in his eyes.
"Yes, they've all been tested and verified." Qian Haoming nodded, then smiled. "This is one of the highlights of our city. It's a museum that maintains its originality. Only Hengdu can compare."
"What if it's fake?" Zhao An suddenly smiled playfully.
"That's impossible." Qian Haoming was a little unsure, mainly because Zhao An was such a versatile talent. Even if he told him he could build a rocket, Qian Haoming wouldn't doubt it.
"Who can really tell the difference between real and fake? By the way, are there any auctions or gardens around here?" Zhao An suddenly became interested. Perhaps these would be great for trading.

"Yes, there are places to gamble on stones at night. Young An, do you want to go to the Antique Garden? They're all about buying antiques. People often come from far away to find treasures. Whether you can find them depends entirely on your skills. If you're interested, there's a gambling ground over there. It's a legitimate one, so you can be assured." Qian Haoming seemed interested and spoke incessantly.

It's not that they don't have an interest, but rather that their interest is too advanced. This hobby of buying and selling antiques requires a lot of money, and if it's a genuine antique, it can indeed fetch a considerable price.
But when it comes to making money, jade is truly the only thing that makes money.

chapters.title: Chapter 688 Antique Aura
paragraphs: Zhao An ignored him and continued walking forward, examining a scroll through the glass. It was a yellowed, ancient scroll, hundreds of years old.
Quietly observing, Zhao An read the description before him. This scroll was from the Han Dynasty, a long time ago, and the paper should have rotted long ago.

At this moment, a staff member was called over and introduced Zhao An. "This is a Rising Sun Post, created by an ancient poet. The anti-corruption technology of that era was quite advanced, using a large amount of sesame oil for soaking and a special graphite for writing. The reason for this posting process is currently unknown, but what is known is that this technology may have been used in the emperor's tomb."

"It was indeed used in tombs, and it was made in a workshop under the Han Dynasty. Anyone who understands this will understand, it's true." Zhao An simply glanced at it and left, still unsure of what the light spots meant.

After wandering around the museum, many artifacts were displayed in glass cases. Some items so decayed that only a speck of iron filings remained could still be called antiques, but without the bright spots on them, they were clearly fake.

"Let's go to the antique market." Zhao An chose not to play with women, but continued on his way. He needed to understand the purpose of the recent bright spots; they wouldn't appear for no reason; they must have a purpose.
"Okay," Qian Haoming said after hanging up the phone, smiling. "There's an antique auction happening. Are you interested, Young An?"
"Then let's go." Zhao An was curious about the auction; he had never experienced one before. Perhaps he could buy something special?

The antique market wasn't far away. The streets were made of ancient bluestone bricks, seemingly purpose-built. This area was divided into specialized markets, seemingly intended to serve a special antiques industry.
The antique market contained a wide variety of items: porcelain, ancient jade, cultural relics, paper, ink, brushes, and inkstones—anything ancient could be sold for money.
Antiques weren't particularly valuable; they were more for collection. When something is valuable, it's very valuable; when it's worthless, it's worthless. It all depends on market demand.
The group arrived by car at the antique market. It was already eight o'clock in the evening, and the lights were still bright.

There were many small rugs around the perimeter, where some merchants displayed their props, covered with small items. There were handmade works, as well as some antique-looking items that looked like antiques.
The streets were bustling with people, including many young and beautiful women.
Zhao An walked straight ahead, looking at the shops around him, but didn't see anything special.
He stopped in front of a street stall. The vendor was a middle-aged man wearing a conical hat, with a very peasant air. "Look around, take a look, and name your price if you like it."
Zhao An squatted on the ground, without moving his hands, and asked, "How much are you selling these things for?"
"Sir, which item are you talking about?" the owner asked with a smile, like a simple farmer, but with a hint of cunning in his eyes.
"What about this?" Zhao An said, pointing to an inkstone. It's used to hold ink, and anyone familiar with calligraphy would recognize it.
"We use this as a table leg support. If you like it, I'll give you a thousand yuan!" The seemingly honest owner quoted a shocking price—a truly outrageous one.
Zhao An didn't object, but nodded. "Yes, I don't see much profit at this price. What about this?" He pointed to a slightly rusty piece of iron.

"This is a fragment of an ancient bronze sword, passed down from generation to generation by our ancestors. Unfortunately, it's broken, and only this fragment remains. You're very discerning, customer. I'll give you two thousand yuan." The owner raised two fingers. He could tell Zhao An had plenty of money, so he asked for the exorbitant price.

"Okay, then I won't buy it." Zhao An smiled, then stood up and left. "Hey, customer, wait a moment. Tell me how much!" the stall owner hurriedly called out to Zhao An. How could he let his hard-earned business be snatched away?
"Two hundred, and you have to bring this round ball," Zhao An said, pointing to the round ball next to him.

The round ball was actually just an ordinary rolling ball, meant to be played with in the palm of your hand. Rolling two balls back and forth in your palm stimulates acupuncture points. It could only be considered a health product.
"Well, customer, you're really good at bargaining." The honest owner could only back down, wrapping the item and handing it to Zhao An.
Zhao An took out five hundred yuan and handed it over. "No need for change, you're very generous. Here's your tip."
After some bargaining, he successfully bought what he wanted. Both items glowed faintly.
No one else could see this glow, only Zhao An could. If it glowed, it must be useful.
"Bronze Sword Fragment: Possesses a vintage aura. Absorbing it increases your perception."
"Jade Orb: Possesses a vintage aura. Absorbing it increases your perception."
Both items share the same description, which is quite intriguing.
Zhao An silently absorbed the aura, then toyed with it in both hands. Once in his hands, it was absorbed.
Instantly, Zhao An's facial features became more acute, allowing him to discern the fine hairs on a woman's skin from fifty meters away.

His facial features were magnified, and his perception was clearly heightened. Even the ability to perceive people, acquired after having sex with Qian Yuling, became especially intense. Qian Haoming, standing behind him, could clearly perceive his inner thoughts, only to wonder why he had done so.

At this thought, Zhao An's eyes grew playful. He handed the bag over. "Jade can be played with like a ball, and this fragment is indeed a bronze sword fragment. I'll give it to you. Let's go and see what the auction is like."
"Oh, thank you." Qian Haoming was a little puzzled, but he still took the bag and handed it to his cousin.
Even off to the side, a beautiful woman in a black dress and stylish thin-strap high heels arrived at the auction with several bodyguards and a close friend.
It was hard to tell what brand the dress and heels were, but they must be very expensive. And the vacant expression on her face clearly showed arrogance.

sentences.text: Zhao An ignored him and continued walking forward, examining a scroll through the glass.
It was a yellowed, ancient scroll, hundreds of years old.
Quietly observing, Zhao An read the description before him.
This scroll was from the Han Dynasty, a long time ago, and the paper should have rotted long ago.
At this moment, a staff member was called over and introduced Zhao An.
"This is a Rising Sun Post, created by an ancient poet.
The anti-corruption technology of that era was quite advanced, using a large amount of sesame oil for soaking and a special graphite for writing.
The reason for this posting process is currently unknown, but what is known is that this technology may have been used in the emperor's tomb."
"It was indeed used in tombs, and it was made in a workshop under the Han Dynasty.
Anyone who understands this will understand, it's true." Zhao An simply glanced at it and left, still unsure of what the light spots meant.
After wandering around the museum, many artifacts were displayed in glass cases.
Some items so decayed that only a speck of iron filings remained could still be called antiques, but without the bright spots on them, they were clearly fake.
"Let's go to the antique market." Zhao An chose not to play with women, but continued on his way.
He needed to understand the purpose of the recent bright spots; they wouldn't appear for no reason; they must have a purpose.
"Okay," Qian Haoming said after hanging up the phone, smiling.
"There's an antique auction happening.
Are you interested, Young An?"
"Then let's go." Zhao An was curious about the auction; he had never experienced one before.
Perhaps he could buy something special?
The antique market wasn't far away.
The streets were made of ancient bluestone bricks, seemingly purpose-built.
This area was divided into specialized markets, seemingly intended to serve a special antiques industry.
The antique market contained a wide variety of items: porcelain, ancient jade, cultural relics, paper, ink, brushes, and inkstones—anything ancient could be sold for money.
Antiques weren't particularly valuable; they were more for collection.
When something is valuable, it's very valuable; when it's worthless, it's worthless.
It all depends on market demand.
The group arrived by car at the antique market.
It was already eight o'clock in the evening, and the lights were still bright.
There were many small rugs around the perimeter, where some merchants displayed their props, covered with small items.
There were handmade works, as well as some antique-looking items that looked like antiques.
The streets were bustling with people, including many young and beautiful women.
Zhao An walked straight ahead, looking at the shops around him, but didn't see anything special.
He stopped in front of a street stall.
The vendor was a middle-aged man wearing a conical hat, with a very peasant air.
"Look around, take a look, and name your price if you like it."
Zhao An squatted on the ground, without moving his hands, and asked, "How much are you selling these things for?"
"Sir, which item are you talking about?" the owner asked with a smile, like a simple farmer, but with a hint of cunning in his eyes.
"What about this?" Zhao An said, pointing to an inkstone.
It's used to hold ink, and anyone familiar with calligraphy would recognize it.
"We use this as a table leg support.
If you like it, I'll give you a thousand yuan!" The seemingly honest owner quoted a shocking price—a truly outrageous one.
Zhao An didn't object, but nodded.
"Yes, I don't see much profit at this price.
What about this?" He pointed to a slightly rusty piece of iron.
"This is a fragment of an ancient bronze sword, passed down from generation to generation by our ancestors.
Unfortunately, it's broken, and only this fragment remains.
You're very discerning, customer.
I'll give you two thousand yuan." The owner raised two fingers.
He could tell Zhao An had plenty of money, so he asked for the exorbitant price.
"Okay, then I won't buy it." Zhao An smiled, then stood up and left.
"Hey, customer, wait a moment.
Tell me how much!" the stall owner hurriedly called out to Zhao An.
How could he let his hard-earned business be snatched away?
"Two hundred, and you have to bring this round ball," Zhao An said, pointing to the round ball next to him.
The round ball was actually just an ordinary rolling ball, meant to be played with in the palm of your hand.
Rolling two balls back and forth in your palm stimulates acupuncture points.
It could only be considered a health product.
"Well, customer, you're really good at bargaining." The honest owner could only back down, wrapping the item and handing it to Zhao An.
Zhao An took out five hundred yuan and handed it over.
"No need for change, you're very generous.
Here's your tip."
After some bargaining, he successfully bought what he wanted.
Both items glowed faintly.
No one else could see this glow, only Zhao An could.
If it glowed, it must be useful.
"Bronze Sword Fragment: Possesses a vintage aura.
Absorbing it increases your perception."
"Jade Orb: Possesses a vintage aura.
Absorbing it increases your perception."
Both items share the same description, which is quite intriguing.
Zhao An silently absorbed the aura, then toyed with it in both hands.
Once in his hands, it was absorbed.
Instantly, Zhao An's facial features became more acute, allowing him to discern the fine hairs on a woman's skin from fifty meters away.
His facial features were magnified, and his perception was clearly heightened.
Even the ability to perceive people, acquired after having sex with Qian Yuling, became especially intense.
Qian Haoming, standing behind him, could clearly perceive his inner thoughts, only to wonder why he had done so.

He handed the bag over.

chapters.title: Chapter 689 The eldest princess of the Fang family?
paragraphs: The auction venue wasn't large, housed in a teahouse. The furnishings were all vintage wooden chairs, and the waiters, dressed in period attire, gave the illusion of stepping back into the past, a true experience of an ancient teahouse.
Finding a table, Zhao An ordered some food and gazed at the stage before him. It wasn't the storyteller's seat, where tea and storytelling were supposed to be enjoyed—this was life in ancient times.
Now, the stage was filled with boxes, and a middle-aged man in a traditional Chinese robe was adjusting a microphone.

Looking around, the guests were all middle-aged and wealthy, with very few young people. The only notable thing was a table to the right, where three young women gathered, sipping tea and chatting from time to time. It was quite a sight.
Zhao An narrowed his eyes and examined the boxes. He couldn't see inside at first, but when he focused, he could vaguely see what was inside. This scene was simply unreal!
This change didn't startle Zhao An. Instead, he calmly took a sip from his teacup. "This must be related to those points of light. Is this what's called spiritual energy?"
Ancient relics often have a certain amount of spiritual energy. This aura makes ordinary people feel comfortable and pleasant when they approach it.
But analyzing it is impossible. Aura is colorless, odorless, and formless. It can only be understood, not expressed in words. Perhaps it's waiting to be discovered by those destined to discover it.

Thinking of this, Zhao An's lips curled up slightly. It seems this world is not a simple place! Or perhaps there are many new and wonderful things yet to be discovered. This spiritual energy is a wonderful discovery!

The items in the box were all toys. Although Zhao An's current perspective couldn't see through everything, he could faintly sense some. They seemed to be some ceramics, some inkstones, and some tea sets!
"Young Master, do you have any research into antiques?" Qian Haoming asked, finally finding some time. He had finally found some time, so he had to quickly establish some connections.
"A little bit," Zhao An smiled. "I understand a little bit."

The host on stage spoke. "Welcome everyone to the Guyunfang auction. Today we're auctioning five items, including an authentic calligraphy and painting by Master Zhang. I won't waste any more words, knowing everyone's passion is focused on the treasure hunt. Okay, let's get to the point."
It was clear the host's skills were quite good; with just a few words, he dispelled the anxious anticipation.
The first item to be offered was a tea set. It was simple and yet exuded a sense of grandeur.

"This is a Ming Dynasty purple clay tea set, weathered by the ravages of time. It was collected by Guyunfang from remote areas. With the master's determination, it dates back to the Tianqi period. The auction starts at 10 million yuan, with each bid increasing by no less than 1 million yuan. Now, 10 million, first bid. Any bids?" The host knocked with a wooden hammer.

No one bid at this point. Zhao An could tell that this teahouse boasted several billionaires with net worths exceeding 5 billion yuan. These are all hidden tycoons, as evidenced by the sturdy bodyguards behind them.

"What do you think, Young Master An?" Qian Haoming smiled and greeted the others. As the eldest son and heir to the Qian family, he certainly had some status. Don't think the title of "coal boss" sounds corny; it's all acquired through wealth, and others wouldn't have the opportunity to be corny.
"Not bad, worth the price. Do you want to bid?" Zhao An nodded, picking up a steamed bun and eating.

"I don't deal in antiques; I don't understand them. But I'd be interested in gambling on stones." Qian Haoming didn't hide the fact that he truly didn't know how to identify antiques. Besides, liquidating antiques is a rather complicated matter; you need to find the right seller to fetch such a high price.

"Let's go to the gambling stone field after this. There should be something there." Zhao An wasn't sure. For him, anything was fine; this time he was out for fun. Besides reaching a partnership with the Qian family, he was also supporting Qian Yuling, telling them that he had taken her in and would fuck her every night. The logistics issues in the north would be handled by the Qian family. These local tyrants were the most convenient and effective at this. Another point was to disassociate themselves from the previous convoy incident, lest the Fang family find another opportunity to smear them.
This kind of business struggle is like this: don't reveal even a hint of weakness, or you'll be pursued relentlessly.

"Okay, they're open all night over there. A lot of jadeite rough is shipped in continuously from the Triangle Area, and this is where the bulk of the consumption comes in." Speaking of gambling on jadeite, Qian Haoming felt quite adept.
As beasts of the coal industry, the Qian family members all loved to gamble, simply for the thrill.
"Aren't we going to the local border areas to gamble on jadeite?" Zhao An inquired.

Qian Haoming whispered, "Not anymore. It's more chaotic over there, so it's better to avoid it. Besides, we've already offended people there, with those targeting the mine owners. So it's much safer in the interior."

This wasn't surprising. Where there's business, there's conflict. It's normal, absolutely normal. As Zhao An and Qian Haoming were talking, the competition for the price had already begun to rise, from ten million to thirty million.
Compared to other antiques, tea sets were clearly superior and more practical.
Ceramics, for example, were merely decorative, but these tea sets were still usable, offering a significantly better value for money.
Soon, the tea set was snatched up by a woman, a very young woman, who paid thirty-five million for it.
Qian Haoming glanced at it and whispered, "That's from the Fang family, the eldest princess, Fang Shuiling."
The mention of the eldest princess reminded Zhao An of a woman, and a faint smile curled his lips. "Is she married?"

"No, I heard she's engaged to the second son of the Huang family. It's a family marriage. So they're both having their own affairs. It's true, she didn't refuse other men's advances, but the next day, Huang Meng had their legs broken." Qian Haoming began to recount the gossip.
"Do you often check into hotels with men? So exciting?" Zhao An piqued. This gossip was clearly quite explosive.

"It's said, yes, but there's also some claim not. Anyway, she's just not to be trifled with." Qian Haoming kept these untouchable women and men in mind, lest he step on a tough nut. Just now, not stirring up trouble didn't mean he was afraid. If he were bullied, he wouldn't hold back!

chapters.title: Chapter 690 Someone is arguing!
paragraphs: That being said, Zhao An could immediately tell Fang Shuiling was still a virgin. Despite her somewhat flirtatious behavior, she was actually a genuine virgin! This was a bit outrageous, having fooled everyone. While a virgin's status could be easily discerned from appearance alone, it was also possible to tell without a trace.
Whether or not she was a virgin had nothing to do with Zhao An. The Fang family and he were currently enemies, and even if she was a beautiful woman, he wouldn't be a sycophant.

"Forget it, let's not talk about her anymore. Let's eat, and then go gamble on stones." Zhao An wasn't focused on the Fang family's eldest daughter. He didn't have any particular desire for women at the moment.

The second item up for auction was a piece of porcelain, sold for 500,000 yuan. This price was over ten or twenty years' income for an average person, but for a wealthy individual, it was barely the price of a meal.
The third item up for auction was an ironware artifact, an ancient iron pestle, utterly decayed. One could only vaguely tell from the exterior that it was perhaps an old item.
And even knowing it was hundreds of years old, such an unremarkable item would be hard to bring to the table.

It's simply unsightly and yields no profit, that's all. It doesn't really matter whether you like it or not. It's like keeping a mistress: if you like it, keep it; if you don't, don't maintain it. It's a simple matter.

"A longsword from the Northern Song Dynasty. As we all know, even iron can't resist the corrosion of time. We brought this longsword back from Northern Song Dynasty ruins. It looks like it belonged to a general. Anyone interested can bid on it. There's no price limit," the auctioneer said calmly.
To be fair, this item is at least two hundred years old, if not hundreds. Furthermore, it's an antique, but the commercial value of such items is shockingly low.

At least paper, ink, brush, and inkstone can be given to the older generation, bringing a touch of scholarly spirit to their gifts. An inkstone, at least, sounds nice and is still usable. What could one possibly do with this junky weapon? Honestly, even if you paid for it, it'd be in the way.
For a moment, the scene was a bit quiet. Zhao An stared at the rusty longsword, gleaming with a faint light. The aura within it was identical to the one he'd seen in the museum.
"Two hundred thousand." Zhao An, not intending to be taken advantage of, simply called out a rather ordinary price.
This price was significantly lower than previous auction items, almost ridiculously low. But it was already quite good. We were thankful it even sold. It was a joke!
When they saw someone bid, everyone turned their heads to look over. They only saw Zhao An, wearing a baseball cap and with his head bowed, making him completely invisible.

Qian Haoming, standing nearby, was well-known. After all, the Qian family was a major player in the coal industry. They'd made their fortunes as coal barons. They didn't have much else to offer, but they had a lot of money!
Fang Shuiling, who had been playing with her phone, glanced over at Zhao An. "Who's that Qian Haoming with?"

"I don't know. He must be a friend. He's a bit pretentious, wearing a hat so late at night. Could he be a cuckold? Haha!" A heavily made-up woman scoffed. In the eyes of these young ladies, unless someone was more powerful than them, they were just laughable.

"Qian Haoming isn't stupid," Fang Shuiling said simply. She knew the history of family feuds. At least the Fang family couldn't control the overall situation, and their relationships with many families with whom they had business conflicts were not very good.
If someone made a bid, someone would naturally follow. While I didn't know what the point was, shouting a few times with all my might was enough to satisfy me.
Even if the other party didn't follow, a few hundred thousand wouldn't be a big deal for anyone present; they could just listen for fun.
"Three million." Zhao An continued to bid, then raised his sign and called out the price again, so he knew who had made the bid.
"Three million, one hundred and ten thousand." A coal boss continued to raise the price without even turning his head.
"Four million!" Zhao An raised the price again.
"Four million!" the coal boss continued to raise the price, as if deliberately trying to tease him.
Zhao An's expression was slightly displeased, and he stared coldly at the fat, greasy-eared guy in front of him. "Five million."
"Five million!" The coal boss's head shrank, as if he sensed a chill, perhaps the air conditioning was too cold.
A faint smile played at the corner of Zhao An's mouth, and he stopped raising the price.
"Young Master An, I'll take care of him," Qian Haoming, standing beside him, immediately offered his courtesy.
"No need. If he wants it, he can take it. Let's go and gamble on the stones." Zhao An sneered, put down his sign, and left.

"Oh, you don't have to be so rude even if you can't afford to lose. It's only five million, who can't afford that?" the coal boss turned around and sneered. He was a lackey of the Fang family and had never been fond of the Qian family. They all came from the coal mining industry, so there was no need to mock each other.
"Tan Chong, don't go too far!" Qian Haoming clearly knew this guy; he was the one challenging them. He was also the cannon fodder sent out by the Fang family.

Tan Chong knew he was just cannon fodder, but fortune is achieved through risk. As long as he could maintain his position as cannon fodder, the subsequent wealth would flow in, something many people dreamed of.
To climb the ladder, besides perseverance, you also need opportunity. It's not something anyone can climb.

"Haha, I'm just being too much. Not convinced? Come and bite me!" Tan Chong laughed heartily, his expression brimming with pride. Since he'd already offended them, he might as well offend them even harder!
"You!" Qian Haoming was also extremely angry. This was clearly a lack of respect!

Zhao An stopped him, sneering, "Let's go. Actually, that thing isn't even worth five thousand. I was just checking to see if there were any idiots who'd fall for it. I didn't expect one to actually do it. By the way, if you have the time, why not go back and check if your son is yours, you cuckolded slave?"
"What did you say?" Tan Chong was furious. He hit someone in the face, what was the point?

Zhao An ignored him, grinning cheerfully as he left. Things he set his sights on would never be taken away from him. Since they were fighting for it, he'd take it first. I'll take it back later, idiot!

Let's go and gamble on the stones." Zhao An sneered, put down his sign, and left.
"Oh, you don't have to be so rude even if you can't afford to lose.
It's only five million, who can't afford that?" the coal boss turned around and sneered.
He was a lackey of the Fang family and had never been fond of the Qian family.
They all came from the coal mining industry, so there was no need to mock each other.
"Tan Chong, don't go too far!" Qian Haoming clearly knew this guy; he was the one challenging them.
He was also the cannon fodder sent out by the Fang family.
Tan Chong knew he was just cannon fodder, but fortune is achieved through risk.
As long as he could maintain his position as cannon fodder, the subsequent wealth would flow in, something many people dreamed of.
To climb the ladder, besides perseverance, you also need opportunity.
It's not something anyone can climb.
"Haha, I'm just being too much.
Not convinced?
Come and bite me!" Tan Chong laughed heartily, his expression brimming with pride.
Since he'd already offended them, he might as well offend them even harder!
"You!" Qian Haoming was also extremely angry.
This was clearly a lack of respect!
Zhao An stopped him, sneering, "Let's go.
Actually, that thing isn't even worth five thousand.
I was just checking to see if there were any idiots who'd fall for it.
I didn't expect one to actually do it.
By the way, if you have the time, why not go back and check if your son is yours, you cuckolded slave?"
"What did you say?" Tan Chong was furious.
He hit someone in the face, what was the point?
Zhao An ignored him, grinning cheerfully as he left.
Things he set his sights on would never be taken away from him.
Since they were fighting for it, he'd take it first.
I'll take it back later, idiot!

chapters.title: Chapter 691 Gambling Stone Field
paragraphs: "I'm sorry, Young Master An, I made your visit unpleasant. It's my fault. For the next gambling on the stones, I'm willing to pay three million to make you happy." Qian Haoming was very polite. He apologized first, then offered to cover part of the expenses. Three million was already a lot; it was just a courtesy.
Zhao An waved his hand. "I don't need the money. Haha, let's go. Don't bother with this guy."

Having made up his mind, Zhao An naturally wouldn't let go of someone who opposed him. He should be cannon fodder, but what's the point of jumping out and showing off? It's just like he's too old to live, right?
Getting into the car, Zhao An smoked cigarettes the whole way, not even making a phone call.

An invisible robot flew in the air. It was the Iron Man suit Zhao An had developed. Fans who have seen the "Iron Man" movies directed by Zhao An would surely exclaim in amazement! This was a real Iron Man suit, not a fictional one!

The Iron Man suit hovered in the air, its target locked on Tan Chong, who was leaving the antique market. It was clear Zhao An was targeting someone who had others pay him, then proceeded to steal the goods.

This kind of behavior was immoral, but when it came to a sworn enemy, it was much more interesting. Moreover, he had just clashed with Tan Chong, and now something bad had happened to him. He would undoubtedly be the first suspect.
Even if Zhao An wasn't suspected, Qian Haoming would be a strong suspect.

This, however, was the shrewdness of Zhao An's gambling on the stone market. The gambling on the stone market was filled with people who could all testify. He simply had to show up at the market and constantly select and cut the stones.
With this alibi, Tan Chong's case had nothing to do with him.
Every move was carefully planned. The group arrived at the gambling on the stone market, and surprisingly, someone from the Fang family also showed up.
This time, it wasn't Fang Shuiling, but Fang Shunli, the heir of the Fang family. This was certainly Qian family territory, but it was also more of a Fang family connection.

The Fang family's headquarters was in Hengdu, but this was the family's birthplace, and the relationships here were intricate. Each generation of heirs needed to return to their roots to develop, learn the inherited skills, and sort out their interpersonal relationships before taking on the mantle.
"That's Fang Shunli, the Fang family's heir, a man more cunning than a demon," Qian Haoming whispered to Zhao An. Compared to him, the Qian family's eldest son held less weight.

What was completely unexpected was that Fang Shunli would actually come over to greet him, seemingly unaware of the business competition between them. "Zhao An, I've heard so much about you, so much about you."
Zhao An, with a forced smile, extended his hand and shook it. "It's just so-so. Young Master Fang is in the mood to come here and play a few rounds. What a coincidence."

"Life needs a little excitement, doesn't it? I heard you've returned to the Bai family. What should we call you now?" Fang Shunli said with a forced smile. As the heir to one of the four great families, he simply looked down on people like Zhao An. Though there was a hint of warmth in his words, one could actually see the amusement on his face.

"If you need excitement, go racing. Accidentally getting killed in a car accident—that's what excitement is. Excuse me, let's go." Zhao An, with a hint of disdain, took the beer beside him and washed his hands, as if shaking hands with such a person were a dirty act.

"You!" A lackey was standing up for his master. Such an insulting gesture was a sign of disdain. How many people would have loved to have a handshake from the eldest son of the Fang family? And how dare you despise it?
Fang Shunli stopped his subordinate and shook his head. "Don't be impulsive. He did it on purpose. Haha, Zhao An, you're quite capable."

The strategy against Zhao An was his own. He couldn't let Zhao An get ahead too easily, especially after knowing he was a member of the Bai family. Even if he was from a side branch, with such talent, he could already be among the core disciples.

Besides, the Fang family and the Huang family were married. Together, they had nothing to fear from each other. Even the Bai family couldn't stand it. One couldn't beat two. One plus one could sometimes be greater than two!

Ignoring the sudden appearance of the Fang family, Zhao An walked straight to the pile of stones. The stones here were measured by weight. The rough stones looked no different, no different from any other stones on the roadside.
Three million yuan might seem like a lot, but in reality, each pound of these stones was worth two hundred thousand, so it wasn't really that much.
Gambling on stones is a matter of heartbeat, and there are also many jades among the stones.
The price of buying finished jade is very high, so large wholesalers generally opt for gambling on jade.
While gambling on jade is certainly lucrative, it can also lead to total loss. It's a matter of one's perspective, whether it's heaven or hell.
For Zhao An, with his clairvoyant powers, he could vaguely see whether there was jade, but he couldn't confirm its quality. He could be certain of its presence, but not its quality.
"Young Master An, I heard this batch of jade isn't very good," Qian Haoming whispered. Half the stones here have been selected by so-called experts, so the chances of finding a good one are slim.

The jade market has always enjoyed a large sales volume. It can be worn at weddings and after childbirth. It's also a top choice for gold and silver jewelry. Jewelry makers are guaranteed to be profitable.
"So-called experts? Do you believe them?" Zhao An sneered, seeming somewhat disdainful.
"I don't believe it," Qian Haoming shook his head. He certainly wouldn't believe it if he didn't gamble on jade.
"Haha, what a coincidence! I didn't believe it either." Zhao An picked up the stone and patted it. "Do you know what a genius is?"
"I don't know. Please teach me, Young Master An." Qian Haoming asked humbly.

"Take the paths of others and broaden your horizons, so you don't take detours or end up in a dead end. Many people say that crossing industries is bad, but it's definitely not. That's because these people are ignorant and superficial." Zhao An suddenly picked up a stone and handed it over. "Put it away. I'll settle the account later."

Qian Haoming handed the stone to his cousin, feeling a tinge of anticipation. "Young Master An, there's a special stone-cutting machine over there. Do you need to come over later? We'll draw the prizes live?"
Zhao An glanced at the machine in the distance and nodded. "Sure! I want to see what raw jade looks like, too."

chapters.title: Chapter 692 Alibi
paragraphs: Elsewhere, Tan Chong, carrying the bronze sword fragments he had photographed, got into his Mercedes-Benz and headed for the gambling stone market. He had received the news. The eldest son of the Fang family had appeared there, and he had to go and show his courtesy.
Two burly bodyguards were also in the car—professional thugs hired for personal protection.
Despite the stable security situation, sometimes bodyguards weren't even necessary. But was that what the wealthy needed? They needed the air of pretense, the air of prestige!

The floating steel armor had locked onto the vehicles on the road. The road to the gambling stone market was a mountainous one, not remote, and there were still a lot of vehicles coming and going. As a gambling stone market, it had always been a popular area.
Using the principles of electromagnetic control, the steering wheel suddenly changed direction and darted into a small road.
Tan Chong sensed something was amiss and immediately shouted fiercely, "Are you drunk? This isn't the right road. Damn it, are you trying to kill me?"
The bodyguard in the passenger seat didn't move at all, instead twitching violently, as if knocked unconscious by the electric shock.
A flash of electricity flashed, using a small stun gun to knock the occupants unconscious.
Iron Man first hacked into the dashcam from outside the car, preserving the recorded video at the previous frame.
After completing this, he took the bronze sword fragment that Tan Chong had collected and left.
After entering stealth mode, Iron Man arrived at the gambling stone field and handed the bronze sword fragment to Zhao An in the restroom.
Wearing white gloves, Zhao An touched the bronze sword fragment and absorbed the spiritual energy within.

Instantly, his clairvoyance increased significantly. Even his perception was heightened once again. This spiritual energy could comprehensively enhance his abilities, strengthening many aspects of his abilities.
After completing all this, Zhao An left the restroom. The entire process took less than a minute.

Iron Man Suit also switched to stealth mode and left, returning to Daben and returning the bronze sword. He also injected Tan Chong with a poison that would force him to have an erection, and then release it continuously, like a god of war.
The result was an extreme high, his penis bleeding profusely, and his entire reproductive organs necrotized, beyond repair.
The method was cruel, but the result was satisfying. To be cruel to the enemy is to be kind to oneself.
After completing all this, Iron Man Suit adjusted the recorder again. The entire process was flawless, even undetectable. The footage remained unchanging, maintaining the coma of several people.

At the same time, he injected the bodyguard driving the car with alcohol, thus confirming the drunk driving accident. This was also a car accident caused by drunk driving. As for the fainting, it was not worth mentioning.
The whole process took less than ten minutes, and Tan Chong awoke. His first reaction was to check the treasures he'd auctioned—they were intact, untouched.
But something seemed off. He smelled alcohol, and in a rage, he slapped the driver on the head. "Fuck you, how are you driving? I'll give you a lesson when we get back!"
The others also woke up dazedly. The sudden impact seemed to have knocked them unconscious.
After checking, nothing was lost. Only the front of the car had flattened, where it had hit a tree.
Tan Chong, who had been preparing to go to the gambling stone field, suddenly felt a surge of sexual desire, seemingly unable to suppress it. "Turn around and go back to the neighborhood."
Uncontrollable, he simply went to a nearby hotel, found a nosy woman, and started having sex.
Inside the gambling stone field, Zhao An's smile grew even more playful. The sheer exhilaration, coupled with the sudden sense of descent into hell, would surely make anyone's heart shatter!
Continuing to gamble on the stones, a man soon arrived. He was pot-bellied and looked like a drunkard.
"Uncle, you're here too," Qian Haoming said first. "Uncle, this is Mr. An, our main partner this time and a major client. Mr. An, and this is my uncle, Qian Zilai."
"Hello, nice to meet you." Zhao An smiled gently. This family was quite interesting. The men's names were a bit clichéd. Qian Ben, Qian Zilai? Interesting.

"Hello, Mr. An. I've heard you're a versatile person. I'm really excited to see you trying your hand at this business today. Mr. An, do you mind if I observe? If I have the right rough, I'll charge you the price." Qian Zilai was a chubby man with the smile of a simple farmer.

"No problem." Zhao An looked over at him, and this time, he was practically transparent. You can see everything inside the raw jade. Many stones are empty, some are only the size of rice grains, and occasionally you'll find jade the size of an egg, with a beautiful color.
The gambling industry is lucrative, and the suppliers are the ones who consistently profit. Simply bringing a truckload of jade from the border is enough to earn a steady income.

The areas where the ore is produced are plagued by years of war, making it impossible to build factories and barely achieving self-sufficiency. Many daily necessities rely on imports, so bringing in groceries and food is a near-perfect investment.

This industry has always been controlled by the Lin family. While the profits aren't particularly lucrative, the Lin family's supply has been stable over the years. They act solely as middlemen, profiting from the price difference, and have little interest in intervening in the jade rough market. This fact hasn't been criticized, so they've kept their control, and nothing matters. As long as they can make money, everything else can be put aside.

In addition to being able to see if there's jade in the stones, Zhao An can also see through people's clothing and see what's going on inside. In his eyes, all the men present were bald, their disguises clear to the naked eye. Women were no exception; the shape of their breasts and the presence of pubic hair were all visible.

If Zhao An had acquired this skill upon his rebirth, he might have been thrilled, seeking every possible means to remove the helmet and satisfy his desires. But now, he felt no wavering, even a little inclined to smile. He had no shortage of women; if he wanted any, he could have sex with them.
It was a novelty, though. This skill was quite good, and could prove useful in crucial moments. There are no useless skills, only people who don't know how to use them.

chapters.title: Chapter 693 Failure or profit
paragraphs: Zhao An quickly began selecting the rough stones, first picking out some valuable ones. Some of the valuable stones were hidden deep within the pile, perhaps by coincidence. So, if he wanted to get to the stones, he couldn't just rummage through them; that would seem too fake.
Unable to expose himself, Zhao An could only randomly select a few. "Okay, that's all. Let's go open the stones. I want to see how much fun this stuff is."
"Come here, come here!" Qian Zilai quickly took over Qian Haoming's position, expressing great enthusiasm for Zhao An.
Actually, the so-called opener is just a slotting cutter, with the lower end modified to accommodate irregular stones.
Looking at the cutter next to him, Zhao An waved his hand. "I'll do it myself."
The cutter didn't mind; many wealthy second-generations enjoyed a little fun. He handed over a pair of goggles. "Okay, but I'll be watching to ensure your safety."
"I don't need yours, I have my own," Zhao An said, pulling out a pair of glasses. With a click, they folded into goggles.
Starting the cutter, Zhao An gripped the handle and pressed down, sending the rotating gears slicing downwards.
Seeing someone cutting a stone, the surrounding onlookers also began to watch the excitement. After all, many weren't wealthy; they were simply there to try their luck.
On the second-floor stands, Fang Shunli sat in a chair, watching like a spectator watching a clown perform below. "Haha, gambling on a stone?"

Zhao An's precise movements cut through a large portion of the stone in one stroke, but the resulting fragment didn't contain a single trace of green. While green isn't a desirable color, everyone in the gambling stone market loves it. It symbolizes jade, income, and money!
"Hush!" Everyone let out a sneer of derision. The onlookers were not afraid to make a scene. After all, the losses were someone else's, not theirs.

However, Qian Haoming and Qian Zilai remained expressionless. They had seen a lot of storms before. This was just a broken record, no big deal. Since it was gambling, nine out of ten losses were inevitable. As long as the winnings recouped their investment, or even exceeded it, that was a profit!
Zhao An ignored the mockery and ridicule. In his opinion, they were all idiots.
He continued to cut with his knife, splitting a bowl-sized stone into four pieces with each stroke.
He carried the stones to the scrap area and then placed them on the shelf. His expression remained silent, as if he was a little overwhelmed.
There were still a dozen or so stones left. He could take his time. There was no need to rush. It was just for fun.
Thinking of this, Zhao An even took out a cigarette, lit it, and controlled the cutting machine with one hand.
"What a nice smell! What kind of cigarette is this?"
"It smells like medicinal herbs."
"This seems to be a kidney tonic?"

The men around were whispering among themselves. Seeing the Qian uncle and nephew present, they didn't dare to act too recklessly. Did they really not consider the village chief a cadre? Fang Shunli could ignore the Qian family because he was the heir to the Fang family, but could anyone else dare to do the same? They were truly clueless, or perhaps they were overly complacent?
Zhao An continued smoking his cigarette. With one stroke of the knife, he sliced the stone in half. He was surprised to see a hint of green, and it looked quite good!
"Green!"
"Holy crap! This can be green?"
Everyone exclaimed in surprise. The previous sneer had become a joke. Others laughed at someone's madness, while others laughed at him for being an idiot!

"Young Master An, there's jadeite here! Do you want me to have one of my craftsmen help you cut it?" Qian Zilai said with a smile, trying to please Zhao An and also to flatter him, to liven up the atmosphere.
"Sure, I'll make a few more cuts." Zhao An, cigarette between his lips, turned the stone and continued cutting.

This scene made everyone around him a little nervous. What if he cut into jadeite? A complete piece of jadeite and a broken piece of jadeite would definitely not be worth the same price! Knowing there was green, it would definitely need to be carefully polished to reveal all the hidden jade, keeping it as intact as possible to sell it for a good price.
Most people are cautious when they see jadeite, but Zhao An was not like that. He continued to work with his knife, acting like an amateur and a fool.

After a few cuts, except for two cuts, nothing was seen. However, green was visible on the other two sides. Overall, there should be about a kilogram of jadeite. Although the quality was average, aquamarine, it was already very good.

"Congratulations, Young Master An! The guaranteed price for this piece of jade is eight million. Leave it to me and I'll polish it, how about that?" Qian Zilai generously offered a price, taking a small cut as a favor.
"Take it and polish it. Eight million? It's barely enough to fill a gap between my teeth. I'm just having fun." Zhao An sneered, his words sounding pretentious.
Is that gap between his teeth like a sewer? Even eight million can't fill it? How wide would that be?
Qian Zilai's face twitched uncomfortably. It seemed like he was the real rich man, completely oblivious to such multi-million dollar deals.

Seeing the quality, Zhao An continued cutting. In fact, he had already made back his investment. The raw material was only worth three and a half million. Even if he cut it all and there were no jade left, he would still have made over four million.

One cut brought over four million yuan. For the average person, that's the price of a house, a car, and a mistress. How could that not be terrifying? How could it not be thrilling? It was incredibly thrilling!
This is why gambling on stone is so exciting. Some people even travel thousands of miles just for the thrill of getting rich overnight.
It's not that there aren't any; there are many. But in unseen places, even more people have lost their entire fortunes, unable to afford loans, and have committed suicide by jumping off buildings.

Zhao An continued to slice the stone with his knife. Just then, the tall Fang Shuiling, in her high heels, walked into the stone gambling field with her best friend and happened to see Zhao An cutting.

Fang Shuiling felt neither disgust nor curiosity towards Zhao An. Even if Zhao An claimed to be able to build rockets, it didn't matter. It had nothing to do with her. What interested her was his current economic status.

Some of the valuable stones were hidden deep within the pile, perhaps by coincidence.
So, if he wanted to get to the stones, he couldn't just rummage through them; that would seem too fake.

"Come here, come here!" Qian Zilai quickly took over Qian Haoming's position, expressing great enthusiasm for Zhao An.

This was just a broken record, no big deal.
Since it was gambling, nine out of ten losses were inevitable.
As long as the winnings recouped their investment, or even exceeded it, that was a profit!
Zhao An ignored the mockery and ridicule.
In his opinion, they were all idiots.

The men around were whispering among themselves.
